name: roleboard-keyvision-person-design-v1
description: Measures whether a roleboard belongs to the key vision's shared character-design and rendering language without copying a depicted identity.

scale.8: strong same-project match with minor differences
scale.10: exceptionally coherent same-project character language with concrete visible evidence

dimensions.question: Does the roleboard use the same stylized 3D/CG rendering family, edge treatment, depth, polish, and finishing level as the key-vision characters?
Do facial planes, feature simplification, eye treatment, nose and mouth construction, age handling, and stylization intensity follow the same design language without copying a specific face?
Do skin smoothness, subsurface softness, highlight rolloff, tonal transitions, and texture restraint match the key-vision character treatment?
Do hair massing, strand grouping, edge softness, highlight behavior, and integration with the head belong to the same rendering family?
Do head-to-body ratio, shoulder and torso construction, limb proportions, posture, and stylization level feel designed for the same project while respecting the role's age and identity?
Do garment silhouettes, layer hierarchy, seam and closure logic, drape, and profile/back readability use the same production-design logic without copying a specific costume?
Do cloth, hair, skin, wood, leather, and metal respond to light with the same restrained material hierarchy and physical coherence as the key vision?
Do hue restraint, saturation, value grouping, warm-cool balance, and accent use belong to the key vision's character palette system?
Do light softness, directionality, facial readability, contact shadows, ambient fill, and atmospheric restraint match the key-vision character presentation?
Does the roleboard match the key vision's balance of readable silhouette, controlled ornament, cultural detail, asymmetry, and non-game-skin restraint?

gates.description: Exactly one front, one true profile, and one back full-body view, with no extra panel.
All three views depict one consistent identity.
Heads, bodies, hands, garments, and feet are complete and usable.
Age, gender presentation, stable facts, wardrobe facts, and role status are not contradicted.
The template's warrior face, crown, hair, armor, sword, costume, body, or white-clay material is not copied.
No concrete key-vision face, hairstyle, costume, prop, pose, or scene is copied as the target identity.
No production-breaking facial, hand, limb, or body defect.
No text, watermark, logo, extra subject, extra prop, or collage artifact.
